papers.title: BPR: Bayesian Personalized Ranking from Implicit Feedback
papers.relevance_notes: Foundational pairwise ranking loss - optimizes 'user prefers A over B' directly instead of pointwise classification. Direct alternative to pointwise BCE on long_view, matching v3's top research priority.

papers.title: PiRank: Scalable Learning To Rank via Differentiable Sorting
papers.relevance_notes: Makes NDCG itself differentiable via a relaxed/soft sort, optimizing something closer to nDCG@5 directly rather than a surrogate like BPR. Good second step once pairwise loss is validated.

papers.title: TF-Ranking: A Scalable TensorFlow Library for Learning-to-Rank
papers.relevance_notes: Library implementing pointwise/pairwise/listwise losses (including LambdaLoss) in one place, with the paper's own results showing listwise > pairwise > pointwise. Lets the agent try several listwise objectives cheaply without writing each from scratch.

papers.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
papers.relevance_notes: Attention mechanism weighs a user's past interactions differently depending on the current candidate item. KuaiRand-Pure gives each user hundreds of chronological interactions - DIN is the standard first step to use that history instead of discarding it.

papers.title: Deep Interest Evolution Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
papers.relevance_notes: Adds a two-layer GRU to model how a user's interest evolves over time, not just which past items are relevant. Natural next step past DIN if plain attention underfits.

papers.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
papers.relevance_notes: Transformer-style self-attention over a user's interaction sequence, no recurrence required. Fast, well-established sequential baseline - good first thing to try before something heavier like BERT4Rec.

papers.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
papers.relevance_notes: Bidirectional Transformer trained with a masked-item objective. Usually stronger than SASRec but heavier to train - good once ranking loss and a lighter sequential model are validated and there is spare GPU-hour budget (Feasibility criterion).

papers.title: Modeling Task Relationships in Multi-task Learning with Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts
papers.relevance_notes: Shared expert sub-networks with a per-task gating network deciding how much to draw from each expert. Standard architecture for using the other KuaiRand feedback signals to help predict long_view.

papers.title: Progressive Layered Extraction (PLE): A Novel Multi-Task Learning Model for Personalized Recommendations
papers.relevance_notes: Adds task-private experts on top of MMoE's shared experts, specifically designed to reduce the seesaw effect between conflicting tasks. The challenge's own primer (docx Appendix A.3) names this seesaw problem explicitly - this paper targets it directly.

papers.title: Entire Space Multi-Task Model: An Effective Approach for Estimating Post-Click Conversion Rate
papers.relevance_notes: Jointly models the full impression-to-conversion funnel to fix sample-selection bias (training only on clicked data but needing to score all impressions). KuaiRand has no purchase label, but the docx's own primer (A.2) notes the same bias structure reappears on post-click signals like long_view.

papers.title: Multi-Task Learning as Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.relevance_notes: Treats multi-task training as finding a Pareto-optimal point across tasks' gradients instead of hand-picking fixed loss weights. Useful as a diagnostic tool to confirm an auxiliary signal is actually helping (not fighting) long_view before committing to a full MMoE/PLE architecture.

papers.title: DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction
papers.relevance_notes: Combines a Factorization Machine with a deep MLP sharing embeddings, no manual feature-crossing needed. The official organizer baseline is already an FM, so DeepFM is the minimal, most direct upgrade path.

papers.title: xDeepFM: Combining Explicit and Implicit Feature Interactions for Recommender Systems
papers.relevance_notes: Adds a Compressed Interaction Network that learns feature crosses at the vector level rather than the bit level. Well-cited middle ground between DeepFM and heavier crossing architectures.

papers.title: AutoInt: Automatic Feature Interaction Learning via Self-Attentive Neural Networks
papers.relevance_notes: Multi-head self-attention over feature embeddings learns which combinations matter, instead of hand-designed crosses. Different interaction mechanism than DeepFM/xDeepFM - useful as a contrast experiment.

papers.title: Counteracting Duration Bias in Video Recommendation via Counterfactual Watch Time
papers.relevance_notes: Reframes watch time as value delivered, using counterfactual reasoning to separate genuine interest from the fact that longer videos mechanically allow longer watch times. Directly targets the duration confound in play_time_ms, from a Kuaishou-adjacent research line.

papers.title: Uncovering User Interest from Biased and Noised Watch Time in Video Recommendation
papers.relevance_notes: Companion/earlier method from the same authors as CWM, correcting watch-time labels for duration bias and noise. Simpler correction to try before CWM's full counterfactual framework.

papers.title: Time-to-Event Prediction with Neural Networks and Cox Regression
papers.relevance_notes: General-purpose survival-analysis toolkit for right-censored outcomes. play_time_ms is right-censored (the video can still be playing when the log cuts off) - gives the agent off-the-shelf, well-tested tooling instead of building censored-regression handling from scratch.

papers.title: Time Interval Aware Self-Attention for Sequential Recommendation
papers.relevance_notes: Extends SASRec by encoding the actual time gaps between interactions, not just their order. Minimal add-on to the sequential-modeling work that also covers recency/temporal dynamics - good combined experiment.

papers.title: Continuous-Time Sequential Recommendation with Temporal Graph Collaborative Transformer
papers.relevance_notes: Models interactions as a continuous-time graph so it can predict at any future timestamp, not just 'next item'. Directly tests generalization across KuaiRand-Pure's train (Apr 8-21) / test (Apr 29-May 8) gap. Heavier implementation lift than TiSASRec - lower priority within this area.

papers.title: KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos
papers.relevance_notes: The paper KuaiRand-Pure itself comes from - explains exactly how the randomized-exposure log was collected and what it is valid for. Non-negotiable include.

papers.title: KuaiRec: A Fully-observed Dataset and Insights for Evaluating Recommender Systems
papers.relevance_notes: Companion near-fully-observed dataset from the same lab studying how exposure bias distorts offline evaluation. Directly useful for sanity-checking whether KuaiRand-Pure's validation metric is distorted by exposure bias.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Off-Policy Evaluation for Ranking Policies under the Cascade Behavior Model
papers.relevance_notes: Statistically corrected estimator for how a new ranking policy would perform, using only logged data from the old policy. The actual technique for turning KuaiRand's randomized-exposure log into a trustworthy off-policy validation signal, not just a source describing the data.

papers.title: Modeling Dynamic User Preference via Dictionary Learning for Sequential Recommendation
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
papers.relevance_notes: Models preference drift from timestamped interaction sequences, complementing TiSASRec time intervals and TGSRec temporal graphs. It is a bounded temporal experiment for the train-to-validation date shift; its TensorFlow 1.x reference code is evidence only, not a dependency to import.

papers.title: Unbiased Learning to Rank with Unbiased Propensity Estimation
papers.relevance_notes: Introduces dual learning of a ranker and exposure propensities from biased logged feedback. It complements the existing doubly robust evaluator: use it only as an advanced, train-only debiasing branch after direct validation gains are established; never use test labels.

papers.title: FiBiNET: Combining Feature Importance and Bilinear feature Interaction for Click-Through Rate Prediction
papers.relevance_notes: Uses squeeze-excitation feature importance and bilinear interactions, a distinct interaction mechanism from DeepFM, xDeepFM, and AutoInt. Test only after ranking-loss or history experiments; it must not be combined with adding organizer-tested static features or with an unrelated capacity increase.
